themes_detail.label: Dead Trees Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Dead and dying trees spiked to 4 complaints THIS WEEK compared to a 1.0 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 300% increase (z-score: 3.46)—signaling a potential public safety and environmental health crisis in Woodhaven/Richmond Hill that warrants immediate investigation into whether storm damage, disease, or maintenance failures are responsible.
evidence: 4 dead/dying tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (300% spike, z-score: 3.46)
Illegal tree damage also spiked: 3 complaints last week vs. 0.5 avg (500% increase, z-score: 3.54)
Community board has repeatedly requested park and building improvements, suggesting infrastructure neglect
reporting_angles: Interview NYC Parks about whether recent storms or disease are killing trees in CD 409; are removal crews keeping pace?
Canvass Woodhaven/Richmond Hill residents to identify specific blocks with dead trees and assess safety risks (falling limbs)

themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Surge
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints exploded to 15 complaints 3 weeks ago compared to a 1.5 weekly baseline—a 900% spike (z-score: 13.5, highest statistical severity in the dataset)—indicating either a major operational change by Uber/Lyft, illegal car services, or enforcement gaps that merit urgent investigation.
evidence: For-hire vehicle complaints: 15 three weeks ago vs. 1.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (900% spike, z-score: 13.5)
This is the single largest statistical anomaly in the entire dataset by z-score
Sustained spike suggests ongoing operational or regulatory issue, not isolated incident
reporting_angles: Interview TLC about what triggered the spike; has a new service launched, or are licensed services operating illegally in the area?
Survey residents on 311 complaints to learn whether they cite illegal street hailing, congestion, or driver conduct
Check with local precinct/council member about whether enforcement actions preceded or followed the complaints

themes_detail.label: Food Safety Spike
themes_detail.summary: Food establishment complaints surged to 7 over the past 2 weeks compared to a 1.6 weekly average—a 331% increase (z-score: 7.72)—suggesting potential public health violations in restaurants or food vendors that could pose risks to residents and warrant health department follow-up.
evidence: Food establishment complaints: 7 two weeks ago vs. 1.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (331% spike, z-score: 7.72)
Timing suggests acute trigger (new vendor, enforcement lapse, or seasonal event) rather than chronic issue
High z-score indicates statistical significance and unusual concentration
reporting_angles: Request Department of Health violation data for CD 409; which restaurants/food vendors are cited most frequently?
Interview health department about whether they've increased inspections or identified a specific violation pattern
Canvass residents about where they filed complaints and what violations they observed (rodents, improper storage, etc.)

themes_detail.label: Hazardous Materials Risk
themes_detail.summary: Hazardous materials complaints spiked to 3 over the past 2 weeks compared to a 0.4 weekly average—a 700% increase (z-score: 3.77)—indicating potential toxic spills, improper waste disposal, or industrial violations that require urgent environmental and safety assessment.
evidence: Hazardous materials complaints: 3 two weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% spike, z-score: 3.77)
Low baseline (0.4/week) makes spike statistically striking and suggests rare, acute event
Proximity to hazmat complaints and illegal tree damage suggests possible environmental degradation
reporting_angles: FOIL 311 complaint details to identify specific locations and substances; cross-check with EPA/DEC databases
Contact NYC Department of Environmental Protection about source investigations
Interview residents near complaint locations about odors, visible contamination, or recent industrial activity

themes_detail.label: Animal Abuse Reports Rise
themes_detail.summary: Animal abuse complaints reached 10 last week compared to a 3.9 weekly average—a 158% spike (z-score: 4.22)—suggesting either emerging neglect or abuse patterns in the neighborhood or increased resident awareness that warrants investigation by animal welfare authorities.
evidence: Animal abuse complaints: 10 last week vs. 3.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (158% spike, z-score: 4.22)
Sharp one-week spike suggests either acute incident cluster or sudden reporting surge
Requires cross-check with ASPCA/NYC Animal Care and Control data to validate and assess severity
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Animal Care and Control about whether they've investigated complaints in CD 409; what types of abuse were reported?
Interview ASPCA and local animal shelters about intake and case patterns from Woodhaven/Richmond Hill
Identify specific locations of complaints and whether they cluster around a particular property or facility
